destination.title: Primordial black holes: origins, survival, dark matter and tests
destination.question: Under which formation, evaporation and environmental assumptions can primordial black holes or their remnants contribute to dark matter, and how can observations and cosmological effects test those scenarios?
destination.summary: A useful family joins formation, population evolution, evaporation constraints and proposed survival mechanisms. Particle alternatives, particle constraints inferred from PBHs, and consequences of already-evaporated PBHs retain distinct targets. Scalar-driven stasis has an alternate home connected through model context.

systems: Primordial black holes and proposed remnants
Particle dark matter and evaporation products where explicitly connected
targets: Formation, abundance, mass distributions and population evolution
regimes: Ordinary, charged, rotating, nonsingular and higher-dimensional models
Early evaporation and present-day signals kept distinct
assumptions: Alternative mechanisms are conditional branches, not jointly required premises
Source-era constraints and adopted astrophysical interpretations remain dated
Ordinary and pre-Swampland work is eligible
conventions: Initial abundance and present dark-matter fraction are distinct targets
A signal explanation does not imply an all-dark-matter population
Dimensions, mass functions and charge conventions remain source-specific
includes: Evaporation constraints and proposed changes to evaporation
PBH-mediated particle constraints and cosmological effects as overlaps
excludes: Treating numerical membership as scientific equivalence
Treating general scalar-driven stasis as a PBH mechanism
Inferring a shared Swampland premise from neighboring sources
Treating announced viability as a current universal result

sources.title: Direct detection of primordial black hole relics as dark matter

evidence.text: Estimate the charged fraction using neutral-to-charged and charged-to-neutral residence times, f_charged = (1 + τ_neutral/τ_charged)^−1. Numerically reimplement charged-lepton emission calculations with the actual small lepton mass and without neglecting black-hole charge.

sources.title: Constraining Primordial Black Hole Abundance with the Galactic 511 keV Line

evidence.text: Integrate the emission rate over positron energies from m_e to 1 MeV and PBH masses from 4 × 10^14 g upward. Evaluate a delta-function mass spectrum and a normalized log-normal distribution to obtain the Galactic injection rate.

sources.title: Primordial Black Holes as a Dark Matter Candidate Are Severely Constrained by the Galactic Center 511 keV $\gamma$ -Ray Line

evidence.text: For a monochromatic mass function, calculate the local injection rate Q(E,r) = [ρ_DM(r)/M_PBH] d²N_e/(dE dt). Integrate over volume and energy, then limit the PBH fraction by requiring the resulting yearly positron injection not exceed 6.3 × 10^50.

sources.title: Neutrino and positron constraints on spinning primordial black hole dark matter

evidence.text: Derive a conservative positron bound by requiring PBH injection not to exceed the approximately 10^50 yr⁻¹ rate inferred for the Galactic bulge. Integrate positron emission over 0.511–3 MeV and over the assumed PBH mass distribution and Galactic region.

sources.title: INTEGRAL constraints on primordial black holes and particle dark matter

evidence.text: Compute Schwarzschild Hawking spectra with BlackHawk, including the spin-1 graybody absorption factor rather than using a pure blackbody. The adopted temperature is T_BH=1/(8πGM_BH), and the photon spectrum peaks near 5.77 T_BH.

sources.title: Primordial black holes from single field models of inflation

evidence.text: Can a single-field inflationary potential generate sufficiently enhanced small-scale curvature fluctuations to produce primordial black holes constituting all dark matter, while retaining agreement with the paper's CMB and LSS constraints?

sources.title: Planck Constraint on Relic Primordial Black Holes

evidence.text: How strongly do Hawking-radiation effects on CMB anisotropies constrain surviving PBHs of mass 10¹⁵–10¹⁷ g, and over which masses do the paper's Planck bounds exceed bounds from the MeV extragalactic gamma-ray background?

sources.title: New cosmological constraints on primordial black holes

evidence.text: How do quark/gluon emission and updated light-element and photon-background observations constrain the initial PBH abundance over 10^9–10^17 g? The paper also reviews constraints extending to much larger, nonevaporating PBHs.

evidence.text: Can critical Higgs inflation, including running of both the Higgs self-coupling and its non-minimal gravitational coupling, produce enough primordial black holes to explain dark matter while satisfying CMB and particle-physics constraints?

sources.title: On the (im)possibility of electrically charged Planck relics

evidence.text: Can compact remnants retain ordinary SM electric charge over cosmological times, accounting for ambient capture, vacuum pair creation, mass dependence, and possible dark-sector or near-extremal exceptions?

evidence.text: Can a dedicated spatial-template analysis of Galactic Hawking-emission photons in 16 years of INTEGRAL/SPI data detect evaporating primordial black holes or constrain their dark-matter fraction near the lower asteroid-mass window?

evidence.text: Historical question of the withdrawn manuscript: can field-theoretic dispersion relations constrain higher-derivative Einstein–Maxwell coefficients so large extremal black holes approach Q/M=1 from above and can decay into smaller charged black holes?

evidence.text: What conditions permit extremal black-hole decay beyond the weak-field EFT regime, and what does the conjectured decay of every extremal black hole imply for strong-field electrodynamics, gauge-coupling running, and candidate Maxwell-sector completions?

sources.title: The String landscape, black holes and gravity as the weakest force

evidence.text: Do causality-favored electromagnetic interactions lower extremal black-hole masses within a specified conserved-charge sector?

sources.title: A Weak Gravity Theorem

evidence.text: Treat the metric as an external source for the QFT stress tensor, constructing graviton pseudo-amplitudes without internal graviton exchange. On-shell photon amplitudes are included through LSZ reduction even if low-energy electromagnetism is emergent.

sources.title: On the black hole weak gravity conjecture and extremality in the strong-field regime

evidence.text: For several charges, the authors use charge-to-mass vectors, convex-hull kinematics, and the triangle inequality. The sufficient condition applies along every fixed charge direction; the necessary decreasing sequence may change direction between steps.

sources.title: The String landscape, black holes and gravity as the weakest force

evidence.text: Combine a weight-one current with an opposite-chirality spacetime derivative and a null plane wave, then impose physical-state consistency.

sources.title: A Weak Gravity Theorem

evidence.text: Use the Weyl anomaly to estimate logarithmic curvature-squared running. For mixed and electromagnetic terms, truncate claimed IR-dominated sums and apply Cauchy–Schwarz to bound interference contributions.

sources.title: A Weak Gravity Theorem

evidence.text: Use twice-subtracted dispersion relations and optical-theorem completeness sums to relate coefficient running to QFT matrix elements. Stress-tensor insertions select angular momentum l=0,2, whereas two-photon intermediate states can carry any angular momentum.

sources.title: On the black hole weak gravity conjecture and extremality in the strong-field regime

evidence.text: Magnetic Einstein equations give ft=fr=f and an integral expression for f in terms of LF. Horizon degeneracy is imposed through dM/drh=0. Renormalization-group and trace-anomaly reasoning relate the strong-field action to running gauge coupling.

sources.title: A Stringy Test of the Scalar Weak Gravity Conjecture

evidence.text: Massless scalars can affect black-hole extremality through gauge couplings and affect probe interactions through derivatives of the probe mass. The effective theory keeps these two mechanisms distinct before imposing a relation between them.

sources.title: Charged black holes in Einsteinian cubic gravity and nonuniqueness

evidence.text: Can four-dimensional Einsteinian cubic gravity minimally coupled to Maxwell electrodynamics support distinct asymptotically flat black holes with identical mass and charge, and how do their horizons, thermodynamics and horizonless counterparts behave?

sources.title: Anomaly induced quantum correction to charged black holes; geometry and thermodynamics

evidence.text: How does the curvature-induced trace anomaly modify the static Reissner–Nordström geometry, extremality boundary, thermodynamics, thermal equilibrium, and charged-shell collapse, particularly near zero charge and Planck-scale mass?

sources.title: The Swampland: Introduction and Review

evidence.text: How should charge and gauge coupling be normalized when comparing particle forces, black-hole extremality and quantum-gravity bounds? Integer matter charges fix a convention that the pure Einstein–Maxwell action does not determine.

sources.title: Weak Gravity Conjecture and extremal black holes

evidence.text: Can charged-particle one-loop corrections to extremal black-hole geometry and entropy diagnose Weak Gravity Conjecture violations, motivate its magnetic cutoff, or reveal the large microscopic entropy suggested for attractive charged matter?

sources.title: A Semiclassical, Entropic Proof of a Weak Gravity Conjecture

evidence.text: The background permits a semiclassical test of a charged scalar whose mass is too large to discharge an extremal black hole along a chosen charge direction. A large radius suppresses curvature while the charge projection q·Q can remain large.

sources.title: The Black Hole Weak Gravity Conjecture with Multiple Charges

evidence.text: The EFT isolates how heavy physics changes black-hole extremality when the only massless matter consists of N Abelian photons. General electric and magnetic charges allow the calculation to probe parity-odd interactions that purely electric solutions cannot detect.

sources.title: Higher-order corrections to mass-charge relation of extremal black holes

evidence.text: What classical background and charge normalization define the extremality shift? The calculation fixes the asymptotic mass and Maxwell flux in static, spherical, asymptotically flat Einstein-Maxwell theory in D>3 dimensions.

sources.title: Higher-order corrections to mass-charge relation of extremal black holes

evidence.text: How does a massless dilaton alter extremality and the no-force condition? In the magnetic GHS background, scalar attraction participates in the classical cancellation, so a corrected mass alone cannot determine the sign of the interaction.

sources.title: Force-free higher derivative Einstein-Maxwell theory and multi-centered black holes

evidence.text: Which four-derivative Einstein–Maxwell interactions admit static multicentered extremal black holes with position-independent energy, and are their force-free constraints stronger than preservation of the extremal mass–charge ratio?

sources.title: CUDA Assisted Swampland and Black Hole Thermodynamics

evidence.text: Can CUDA-assisted horizon and thermodynamic calculations connect electric charge, mass and scalar-modulus values to weak-gravity-conjecture bounds and stabilization of charged black holes?

sources.title: Black holes with electroweak hair: The detailed derivation

evidence.text: Linearization around magnetic RN in unitary gauge decouples the charged W perturbation into a complex Proca equation. Angular separation gives a radial Schrödinger problem; negative eigenvalues diagnose instability and zero modes locate bifurcations. Multiple shooting constructs radial modes and nonlinear spherical solutions.
